lesson.grammar_point: expressing preference with prefer and I like it better

listenings.text: Good evening, everybody. Before you order, let me tell you about tonight, because three things are not on the menu. The first is a salmon that arrived this morning, and the chef serves it grilled with lemon and rice. It is not spicy at all, so it is good for children too. The second is a cold noodle dish with vegetables, and it is the only one on the menu that is completely vegetarian tonight. And the third is a small sushi set for people who do not want raw fish: everything in it is cooked, and it is the one I recommend for families. About the spicy ramen on the menu: it is genuinely very spicy, so please ask me before you order it for a child. Forks are always available, and nobody has to use chopsticks. Thank you.

Hello, this is the Sakura restaurant, returning your call about Saturday evening. We have a table for four at half past seven, next to the window, as you asked. Two things about what you told us on the telephone. First, the nut allergy: I spoke to the chef this morning, and the sushi, the salmon and the chicken katsu have no nuts at all. The only dish with nuts is the cold noodle one, so we simply will not bring it near your table. Second, you asked if the children can have something not raw. Yes, of course: we do a small cooked set for children, with rice, and it is nine pounds. If your son prefers, the chicken katsu is also cooked, and most children choose that one. Forks come with every table, so please do not worry about the chopsticks. See you on Saturday at half past seven.

extra_audio.text: Good evening. Two miso soups to start, please. Is the fish raw? I prefer the grilled salmon, because it is not spicy. And a fork for the children, please. Thank you very much.

reading.rtitle: Sakura -- a note for our guests
paras: Welcome to Sakura. Many of our guests come to a Japanese restaurant for the first time, so here is a short note. If you already know this food well, please skip it and order what you love.

Not everything here is raw. The sushi and the sashimi are raw fish, and that is how they should be. But the katsu, the grilled fish, the ramen and the tempura are all cooked, and we always have a cooked set for children.

Spicy is a different question. Only two dishes on our menu are really spicy, and both say so under the name. If you are ordering for a child, please ask us first, because "a little spicy" is not the same in every country.

Chopsticks are on every table, and so are forks. Nobody here thinks less of you for asking for a fork. And if you have any allergy, tell us before you order and not after — the kitchen can change almost any dish, but only before it is made.
reading.source: Note on the table -- Sakura, Japanese kitchen
